t.pt: ทางไหน: por onde se vai
t.en: ทางไหน: asking the way

e.pt: O tailandês pergunta o caminho com ทาง ('caminho, direção') colado no ไหน ('qual'): ไปรษณีย์กลางไปทางไหนครับ, ao pé da letra 'o Correio Central vai por que direção?'. Repare que o ไป vem antes do lugar — é o nosso 'como se chega a X', e não 'onde fica X'. A resposta curta do livro é ตรงไปข้างหน้าครับ ('reto, à frente'); quando é preciso virar, entra o เลี้ยว — เลี้ยวขวา ('vire à direita') — e o destino final vem com อยู่ทางซ้ายมือของคุณ ('vai ficar à sua esquerda'), em que ทาง + lado monta o 'para o lado de'. O มือ ('mão') e o ของ ('de') ali são opcionais, tanto que o livro os imprime entre parênteses: ทางซ้ายคุณ também serve.
e.en: The way is asked with ทาง 'way, direction' glued to ไหน 'which': ไปรษณีย์กลางไปทางไหนครับ 'which way does one go to the main Post Office?', with ไป coming before the place. Short answer: ตรงไปข้างหน้าครับ 'straight ahead'. Turns use เลี้ยวขวา 'turn right', and the final spot is given as อยู่ทางซ้ายมือของคุณ 'it will be on your left', where ทาง + side builds 'toward the ... side'. มือ and ของ are optional there — the book prints both in parentheses — so ทางซ้ายคุณ works too.

t.pt: ข้าง- congela o ponto de vista em quem fala
t.en: ข้าง- fixes the point of view on the speaker

e.pt: O VOCABULARY da lição põe dois conjuntos lado a lado: หน้า ('frente; rosto'), นอก ('fora'), หลัง ('atrás') e as formas com ข้าง — ข้างหน้า ('à frente, adiante'), ข้างใน ('lá dentro'), ข้างนอก ('lá fora'), ข้างหลัง ('a parte de trás'). O ข้าง ('lado') já embute o ponto de vista de quem fala, e por isso a palavra vem pronta: อยู่ข้างในครับ é 'fica lá dentro' sem precisar dizer dentro de quê. Já o substantivo nu pede uma referência do lado de fora — หน้าโรงเรียน, 'na frente da escola'. É o contraste entre o nosso 'aí dentro', que se basta, e 'dentro do prédio', que precisa do complemento.
e.en: The vocabulary sets two groups side by side: หน้า 'in front; face', นอก 'outside', หลัง 'behind' and the ข้าง- forms ข้างหน้า 'ahead', ข้างใน 'inside', ข้างนอก 'outside', ข้างหลัง 'the back'. ข้าง 'side' already carries the speaker's point of view, so the word stands alone: อยู่ข้างในครับ 'it's inside', with no need to say inside what. The bare noun, by contrast, needs an outside reference — หน้าโรงเรียน 'in front of the school'.

t.pt: ออกมา × ออกไป: sair para cá ou para lá
t.en: ออกมา × ออกไป: coming out vs. going out

e.pt: O mesmo verbo muda de sentido pela partícula que vem atrás: ออกมา é 'sair para onde eu estou' e ออกไป é 'sair para longe de mim'. มา aponta para quem fala, ไป aponta para fora — e a direção é obrigatória, o tailandês não deixa o movimento no ar. É o nosso 'vem cá' × 'vai lá', só que grudado no verbo. O diálogo mostra o espelho disso com เดินตรงเข้าไปข้างใน ('ande reto para dentro'), em que เข้า é 'entrar' e o ไป empurra a ação para longe de quem dá a instrução.
e.en: The same verb shifts meaning according to the particle that follows it: ออกมา 'come out' (toward the speaker) versus ออกไป 'go out' (away from the speaker). มา points to the speaker, ไป away — and the direction is obligatory, Thai does not leave the motion unspecified. The dialog mirrors this with เดินตรงเข้าไปข้างใน 'go straight in', where เข้า 'enter' plus ไป pushes the action away from the person giving directions.

notas.ex: เดิน|dəən ตรง|dtrong เข้า|kâo ไป|bpai ข้างใน|kâang-nai

t.pt: ทราบไหมครับ: embrulhar a pergunta por educação
t.en: ทราบไหมครับ: wrapping the question politely

e.pt: Em vez de soltar ที่ส่งโทรเลขอยู่ตรงไหน ('onde fica o lugar dos telegramas?'), o livro embrulha a pergunta no fim: ...อยู่ตรงไหนทราบไหมครับ, ao pé da letra 'onde fica, o senhor sabe?'. O ทราบ é o 'saber (um fato)' formal, o que se usa com estranhos e com superiores — entre amigos seria รู้. E o ไหมครับ no fim suaviza mais um pouco: você não cobra a resposta, pergunta se a pessoa a tem. É exatamente o nosso 'por acaso o senhor sabe onde fica...?', em que a cortesia está em fingir que a outra pessoa pode não saber.
e.en: Instead of a blunt ที่ส่งโทรเลขอยู่ตรงไหน 'where is the place to send telegrams?', the dialog wraps the question at the end: ...อยู่ตรงไหนทราบไหมครับ 'where is it, do you know?'. ทราบ is the formal 'to know (a fact)', the one used with strangers and superiors where friends would say รู้, and the final ไหมครับ softens it further — you ask whether the person knows rather than demanding the answer, just like English 'would you happen to know where ... is?'.
